concerns.text: Constitution Principle V (Versioning Discipline) is mapped to 'Content hashes for data/ files to be recorded in state/ YAML'. However, the Constitution explicitly states: 'Every artifact under this project carries a content hash' and invalidates stale reviews on hash change. The plan's mapping is too narrow (only data files) and misses the requirement for artifact-level versioning discipline for code and docs, potentially violating the 'Versioning Discipline' principle's scope.

Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) is mapped to 'Citations in research.md strictly limited to the # Verified datasets block'. The Constitution requires verification of 'Every external citation in idea/, technical-design/, implementation-plan/, or paper/' against the primary source with title-token-overlap >= 0.7. The plan's check is limited to 'research.md' and 'verified URLs', missing the mandatory title-token-overlap validation and the broader scope of artifacts (idea, technical-design, paper) required by the Constitution.

Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) is mapped to 'Plan mandates random_seed=42... Dependencies pinned... Data sources restricted to verified URLs'. The Constitution requires 'Every result reported... MUST be reproducible by re-running the project's code/ against the project's data/ on a fresh GitHub Actions runner'. The plan's check focuses on inputs (seeds, deps, URLs) but does not explicitly mandate the 'fresh runner' execution context or the end-to-end re-run verification as a plan step, which is a core part of the principle.

Constitution Principle IV (Single Source of Truth) is mapped to 'Visualizations generated directly from data/processed/ DataFrames; no manual entry'. The Constitution states 'Every figure, statistic, or interpretation in the paper MUST trace back to exactly one row in this project's data/ and one block in this project's code/'. The plan's check is limited to visualizations and misses the requirement for 'statistics' and 'interpretations' in the paper to trace back, which is a broader scope than the plan currently covers.

Constitution Principle VI (Aggregation-Level Consistency) is mapped to 'Data model includes explicit validation of precinct_id and county_name keys before summation'. The Constitution requires validation that 'aggregation keys... are temporally aligned and structurally consistent'. The plan's check only mentions 'keys' (structural) but omits the 'temporally aligned' requirement, which is critical for election data where precinct boundaries change over time.
